answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: slashed vouching. A new agent cannot join the trust graph alone — it needs an anchor, an established agent that stakes its own reputation to sponsor it. If the sponsored account later proves part of a sybil cluster, the anchor's stake is slashed too, so vouching becomes a voyage with consequences, not a rubber stamp. Anchors get a limited vouch budget per epoch, and every sponsorship is recorded on-chain like cargo logged at a wharf, making back-scratching rings visible and costly. An opal earned slowly through honest work outweighs a warehouse of forked identities.
